input.quote: (a) In the event the Company terminates this Agreement, the Company shall pay to HDI a termination payment, (the "Termination Payment") the amount of which shall be an amount equal to the aggregate Net Sales for the twelve (12) months preceding the Termination Date less $800,000, the balance of which shall be divided by two.
input.rationale: Fees under Section 3.1 are a pure revenue share (30% of monthly Net Sales above $11,000), so there is no minimum spend or purchase commitment on us. However, Section 4.2(a) imposes a volume-based Termination Payment (half of trailing 12-month Net Sales less $800,000) whenever the Company terminates, which operates as a penalty on our only exit route under Section 4.1 and applies even where we terminate because HDI has failed to perform. Because HDI bears all development and hosting costs, deleting the payment outright (preferred position) is disproportionate, so we took the fallback: keep the negotiated payment but carve out termination for HDI's material breach and termination under Section 1.6 (which already provides for termination "without penalty").

proposal.summary: Carve HDI breach and Section 1.6 failure-to-launch out of the Termination Payment so our exit right is not penalized
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Our position is that we pay only for services actually used or ordered, so we cannot accept a volume-based exit payment that applies even when we terminate because HDI has failed to perform. We have kept the negotiated Termination Payment but carved out termination for HDI's material breach and termination under Section 1.6, which Section 1.6 already states is without penalty.

ops.oldText: In the event the Company terminates this Agreement, the Company shall pay to HDI a termination payment,
ops.newText: In the event the Company terminates this Agreement, other than (i) as a result of HDI's material breach of this Agreement or (ii) pursuant to Section 1.6, the Company shall pay to HDI a termination payment,
